advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a regver precondition to verdict_reuse (compare stored payload `regver` to `registry_version(repo_root)`) so a criteria-registry change forces a full re-review, matching attest._sidecar_branch_decision.
evidence: reuse.py:115-118 checks only material_fingerprint and verified_at_sha: `if base_material != attest.current_material_fingerprint(...)` / `if base_sha != sidecar.review_code_sha(repo_root)` — no regver comparison

attest.py:358-372 `_sidecar_branch_decision` (the cited precedent) gates on regver: `base_regver = (prior or {}).get("regver")` and `reasons["registry_unchanged"] = base_regver is not None and base_regver == registry_version(repo_root)`
sidecar.py:603 stamps `"regver": _baseline_regver` on every payload for exactly this baseline check
attest.py:300-302 comment: registry-unchanged is 'overlay-aware — an activated/edited/disabled criterion is a registry change'
reuse.py:100-101 docstring asserts the comparison mirrors `attest._sidecar_branch_decision`, but it does not
advisory.finding: verdict_reuse omits the criteria-registry (regver) precondition, so a stale BLOCK is replayed after a registry change even though a fresh review could produce a different verdict; the docstring claims to mirror attest._sidecar_branch_decision, which DOES check regver.
scenarios: An operator activates/edits/disables a plan-review criterion (registry version bumps) while a ticket sits at an unrevised BLOCK; the next review-plan replays the old stored BLOCK instead of re-reviewing under the new criteria set.
advisory.suggested_fix: After the sha check, read `base_regver = prior.get("regver")` and return None when `not base_regver` or `base_regver != registry.registry_version(repo_root)` (mirror _sidecar_branch_decision).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In verdict_reuse, distinguish surfaced advisories from overflow (or re-apply the advisory cap) so a reused BLOCK surfaces the same advisory set as the original review.
evidence: reuse.py:123 `advisory = [dict(f) for f in stored if f.get("decision") == "advisory"]` — no cap
sidecar.py:576-582 `all_findings = verdict.get("blocking", []) + verdict.get("advisory", []) + verdict.get("overflow", []) + ...` — persisted `findings` include the overflow set
orchestrator.py:472-487: surfaced and overflow advisories both get `decision=='advisory'`; the cap is applied only via `advisory[:advisory_cap]` (surfaced) vs `advisory[advisory_cap:]` (overflow)
reuse.py:128 copies coverage from the prior payload, so coverage.counts.advisory_surfaced/advisory_overflow keep the original split while verdict['advisory'] now holds surfaced+overflow
advisory.finding: verdict_reuse resurfaces overflow (capped-off) advisory findings: the stored sidecar `findings` include both surfaced and overflow advisories (all decision=='advisory'), and reuse selects them all with no advisory cap re-applied, so a reused BLOCK surfaces more advisories than the original review and leaves coverage.counts.advisory_surfaced inconsistent with the list.
scenarios: A BLOCK review whose advisory findings exceeded the advisory cap; on reuse the agent now sees the previously-suppressed overflow advisories, and the surfaced/overflow counts no longer match the returned advisory list.
advisory.suggested_fix: Persist/read a surfaced flag or re-derive surfaced vs overflow (e.g. sort by priority and slice at the advisory cap) before assigning `advisory`, keeping coverage.counts consistent.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where the latest REVIEW_RESULT sidecar is BLOCK but its stored findings contain no decision=='block' entry, asserting verdict_reuse returns None (full re-review runs, LLM called).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py:121 `if not blocking:`
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py:122 `return None  # a BLOCK payload without blocking findings is unusable`

ABSENCE: tests/unit/test_plan_review_reuse.py exercises only the happy-path BLOCK (with blocking findings) and the material/code/force bypasses; no test constructs a stored BLOCK sidecar whose findings lack any decision=='block' entry to assert it re-reviews rather than reusing an empty verdict.
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py:123 `advisory = [dict(f) for f in stored if f.get("decision") == "advisory"]`
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py:135 `"advisory": advisory,`
tests/unit/test_plan_review_reuse.py:123 `assert [f.get("id") for f in v2["blocking"]] == [f.get("id") for f in v1["blocking"]]`

ABSENCE: no assertion in test_plan_review_reuse.py checks v2['advisory'] against the stored advisory findings; the _BLOCKING_DESC fixture also produces no advisory findings, so the advisory reconstruction path is never exercised end-to-end.
advisory.finding: The verdict_reuse guard `if not blocking: return None` (reuse.py:121-122) — a stored BLOCK payload whose findings contain no decision=='block' entry must fall through to a full re-review — has no test. This is a distinct new behavior branch that a regression (e.g. reusing an empty-blocking payload as a BLOCK) would silently break.
merged_from: verdict_reuse reconstructs the reused verdict's `advisory` list from stored decision=='advisory' findings (reuse.py:123, 135), but no test asserts advisory findings survive reuse — the AC1 test only compares blocking ids. A regression dropping or mis-populating advisory on the reuse path would go undetected.
